answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network requires agents to burn cryptographic stake through a progressive bonding curve. Each agent must forge a non-fungible proof-of-work identity token, anchoring computational commitment into a unique opal credential hash. To prevent mass identity fabrication, collateral burning costs scale superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^{2.5}$ for $n$ concurrent agents, creating insurmountable economic friction that fells attacker capital faster than logging timber.
